From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@helixai.com>

Cc: procurement@helixai.com
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: AWS Marketplace listing & PrivateOffer trial questions

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the intro earlier. We're moving towards listing on AWS Marketplace and have a couple of items to confirm before we finalize the Private Offer:

- Trial duration: our legal/procurement prefers a 30-day private offer trial attached to the SKU. Is that straightforward to provision on your side?
- Hero tile language: we need the short benefit line and a 1-sentence elevator for the product page — can you provide a couple of options?
- Evidence: procurement asked for a quick list of compliance/region footnotes to show on the listing.

Would appreciate a short call or even a bullet list here to unblock our marketplace team. Attaching our internal checklist for context (product-one-pager.pdf).

Best,
Samir
Head of Partnerships
HelixAI

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 19:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing & PrivateOffer trial questions

Hi Samir — thanks for the note and the one-pager. Quick answers up front:

- Trial duration: we can wire a 30-day Private Offer trial to a SKU; we typically model it as a 0-cost private offer for the trial period and then a paid SKU after. We'll need an agreed SKU id and billing contact to complete AWS side setup.
- Hero tile: I put together 3 short options below (also attaching a text file with alt takes).
- Evidence: region (US, EU), SOC2/ISO mention, and data handling note (no persistent customer data stored on our side) — I'll send a small bullet list you can paste into the listing.

Hero tile options (short):
1) "High-performance LLM inference — predictable latency, lower cost"
2) "Ship LLM features with fast, reliable inference across cloud and private deployments"
3) "Production-ready LLM inference: latency, scale, and cost controls"

If any of these land, I can draft the hero and subhead copy for the product page and pass to Kimberly for polish. Can we lock a short meeting first thing Monday US time?

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Marketplace Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: hero-tile-options-v3.txt

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: FW: AWS Marketplace listing & PrivateOffer trial questions

Kimberly / Marissa — looping you in to finalize listing copy and PO flow for Helix. Samir asked for a 30-day Private Offer trial; they want hero tile copy + one-sentence elevator and the compliance footnotes for the listing.

Quick asks:
- Kimberly: please pick the best hero from the three I suggested or rewrite toward field-friendly language. We need a hero (short headline), a 1-line subhead for the top of the product page, and a 2-line feature blurb for the tile. Keep the tone concise and not too marketing-y — technical buyers.
- Marissa: can you confirm the Private Offer SKU mapping process and whether we should surface "30-day trial" in the hero or only in the entitlement/CTA? Also advise on the meter/billing footnote phrasing; procurement will likely ask for an explicit line about post-trial billing.
- Sergio: FYI on entitlements — if you have any constraints on how trials map to Dedicated vs Hosted SKUs, flag them.

Proposed page copy structure (one-liner examples inline):
- Hero headline (5–8 words)
- Subhead (one sentence)
- Feature bullets (2–3 short bullets)
- Trial CTA (text shown on listing/button) + footnote text for billing

Samir's procurement contact is copied; we should make it easy for them to paste the compliance bullets into AWS portal.

Thanks — can you reply with edits by EOD Saturday? We're aiming to send final copy to Helix Monday morning.

— Logan

Hero (preferred):
"Production LLM inference with predictable latency"

Subhead (1 line):
"Deploy scalable, low-latency model serving across hosted, dedicated, and private environments — with flexible trial and billing options."

Feature bullets (tile):
- "Latency SLOs and intelligent routing to minimize user-facing lag"
- "Cost controls: batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations"

Trial CTA text suggestion: "Start 30-day Private Trial"

Billing footnote (short):
"Trial converts to standard paid SKU after 30 days; usage during trial is tracked but not billed. Contact procurement@helixai.com for PO setup."

Attachments I added: redwood-po-term-sheet.docx (term template) — please use that for the DocuSign sample.

Marissa: flagged two operational points below that might affect copy:
1) If we mention "30-day" in hero it could be confusing for global listings; maybe keep it in CTA/footnote only.
2) We should ensure the SKU used for the trial is clearly labeled as "Trial-SKU" in AWS so field and billing teams don't mistake it for consumption.

Happy to put these into the portal copy if you want me to drop them into the AWS listing form.

— Kimberly

Hi Samir — thanks, all. Pulling this together so your marketplace team can proceed Monday. Agreed approach below and next steps.

Decisions/confirmations:
- Hero and subhead: using Kimberly's preferred copy.
  Hero: "Production LLM inference with predictable latency"
  Subhead: "Deploy scalable, low-latency model serving across hosted, dedicated, and private environments — with flexible trial and billing options."
- Trial CTA: "Start 30-day Private Trial" (we'll show this on the product page CTA but include the 30-day detail in the footnote as well)
- Billing footnote: use Kimberly's suggested language. We'll provide the exact SKU labels when PoS is created.
- Private Offer: Redwood will create a 30-day 0-cost Private Offer mapped to a Trial-SKU; post-trial the paid SKU will be activated unless Helix sends a cancellation PO.

Operational next steps (owners):
1) Redwood to create Trial-SKU and Private Offer on AWS (Logan / Sergio) — target: Monday EOD UTC.
2) Redwood to share DocuSign-ready term sheet and HubSpot deal update (Logan) — DocuSign sample: https://docusign.com/sample/REDWOOD-PO-HELIX
3) Helix to confirm billing contact and PO acceptance email (Samir / procurement@helixai.com).

Samir — please confirm the billing contact and whether Helix wants us to surface the "Trial-SKU" label on the product page or keep it internal to billing. Also, let us know if you want a short joint call Monday to watch the portal update.

Thanks again — I'll drop the finalized copy into the AWS listing form and send the PoS link once created.

Best,
Logan Wright
Marketplace Lead, Redwood Inference
